title: Rabbi Acha, Brother of Rabbi Yose of Barkatya
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: “He was [in attendance] before Rabbi Yaakov bar Acha” — so it is cited in Yuchasin, and Seder HaDorot wrote, “I have not found any record of him.” The conjecture of the Gaon, author of Nachal Eden, is that Yuchasin meant Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 2:2, where its reading was “Rabbi Yose went up mi-Barkatya,” and he thought it was a place-name. The reading Hyman uses is “Rabbi Yose went up mevakarteih” — that is, Rabbi Yose came to visit his brother, who was ill, as related there.

notes.text: היה לפני is rendered attendance before Rabbi Yaakov, without inventing earlier chronological priority. The supplied Jerusalem Talmud Bava Batra 2:2 remains alongside saved Guggenheimer 2:3: Rabbi Avdumi is the sick brother whom Rabbi Yose visits. That named witness supports the visiting sense while differing from the Acha headword; Nachal Eden’s explanation remains a conjecture.
